definition: The one measure a pack divides every other dimension from: for an order, the column's semidiameter or diameter; for other packs, a brick course, a structural bay, a room's breadth or a door's width; for the classical trim family, the finished ceiling height.
analogy: Like the scale bar on a drawing: set it, and every other length follows.
more: Authorities do not share a module: Vignola and Chambers measure in the column's semidiameter and Palladio in its whole diameter, so orders are compared at a common column diameter, never at a common module.
basis: Our wording of the pack schema's module field, the modules the packs themselves name, and the grammar layer's module trap. schema/proportion-pack.schema.json, module.name description: "What one module IS: 'semidiameter of the column at its base', 'one brick course including joint', 'one structural bay'."; schema/proportion-pack.schema.json, module.diameters description: "0.5 for Vignola's and Chambers's semidiameter, 1.0 for Palladio's whole diameter."; proportions/systems/room-harmonic.json module.name: "The short dimension of the room in plan - its breadth - from which the length and then the height are both generated"; proportions/systems/opening-proportion.json module.name: "The width of the principal door leaf - the single most fixed dimension in a building"; proportions/systems/trim-classical.json module.name: "The finished ceiling height of the room, finished floor to finished ceiling - the wall the whole trim family is a division of"; docs/proportion.md: "choose Tuscan and a module, and roughly two hundred subordinate dimensions follow deterministically"; docs/proportion.md: "Authorities do not share a module, and getting this wrong silently doubles or halves every dimension an overlay inherits."; docs/proportion.md: "Comparisons are made at a common **column diameter**, never a common module.".
